why:
RFC-0047 / phase 273. The group decides which `SchedContext` the callback runs under -- which RTOS priority tier, and the deadline policy when it overruns. Same verdict and same reason as `rust:SchedContext`: rclrs 0.7.0 has NO callback groups at all (measured: zero `CallbackGroup` / `callback_group` identifiers in the recorded surface -- its isolation primitive is `Worker`, `rust:Node::create_worker`, which is `declined` here), and rclcpp's callback groups carry CONCURRENCY rules and no priority, so neither library has the concept this takes. On a PUBLISHER the group has no scheduling effect today and the row says so rather than implying one: a publisher carries no executor-dispatched callback slot, since `publish()` is driven by the user. It exists for symmetry with the subscription and timer forms and for the intra-process / loaned-message knobs that would use it.

On `nros::Node`, the executor-borrowing node handle (`exec.node_mut(id)`); it was `NodeCtx` until phase-483 W2, which the correlator folded onto `Node` (`TYPE_SYNONYMS`). MEASURABLE ONLY SINCE 2026-09-12: `nros_node::executor`'s `mod node` kept the type private while `Executor::node_mut` returned it, so every method on it was callable and none of them had ever produced a row -- issue 1351.
